messages:
Sasha: heads up - saw a pretty subtle correctness blip from the KV cache in prod during a long-context replay test. some tokens at the start of responses looked like leftovers from previous requests.
Anika: can you paste a short repro or logs? sounds like cross-request contamination, but curious if it's alignment or stale blocks.
Sasha: repro attached (small loop hitting same model with varying lengths). logs show page slot reused without updating start_token_idx. snippet: ```
[INFO] alloc_page slot=42 start_token=120 gen=17 tag=0x7f
[WARN] attach_request slot=42 observed_skip=1 expected_start=121 actual_start=120
```
Sasha: observed when eviction+prefetch race hits: prefetch writes new blocks then eviction path reassigns slot before updating header atomically.
Tim: hmm. we recently merged the slot-reuse optimization that skips zeroing headers for perf. could be an ordering bug.
Jordan: @Anika can you check the allocator code in kv_page_manager? I remember a change to avoid atomic store on start_token to reduce cacheline churn.
Anika: looking now. quick read: allocation sets header.start_token = new_start; then sets tag/gen last. if prefetch writes parts of page concurrently, readers might see partial header. not surprising.
Maria: is this only visible under long contexts / long-lived sessions? any memory growth?
Sasha: two symptoms: 1) occasional wrong token alignment -> model reads stale KV entries producing gibberish; 2) memory growth over long contexts (24h run showed ~12% growth) from fragmentation when slots are reallocated without proper tombstones.
Tim: we should add a request-scoped generation id and require readers to check generation+tag pair before trusting page contents. also reintroduce a fast-path atomic fence on header commit.
Anika: agree. proposed quick patch: on page free -> increment global slot_epoch, store epoch in header with release semantics; on attach -> load epoch (acquire) and verify header.start_token is from same epoch before use. fallback to re-fetch from disk on mismatch.
Sasha: repro command I used: ```bash
for i in {1..2000}; do ./tools/kv_stress --model gptx --len $((100 + (i%250))) --prefetch 4; sleep 0.01; done
```
Sasha: can also trigger with our smoke harness: curl -X POST /v1/generate ... repeated with varying seed.
Jordan: let's prioritize a small safe fix (atomic fence + test) and then optimize. Tim - can you pick up the patch?
Tim: will take it. plan: add header.epoch (u64), use atomic_store_explicit(..., memory_order_release) on commit, readers use acquire and compare. add unit test that races allocator/prefetch using stress harness.
Anika: I'll write the unit test and a deterministic fuzz that flips prefetch timing to reproduce in CI. also adding a canary config to route 1% of traffic to a locked-header build.
InfraBot: perf-runner queued job #4429 for branch/tok-align-fix with tests.
Sasha: thanks. follow-ups: add metrics for slot reuse rate and stale-read counters; alert if stale-read > 0.01% over 5m.
Maria: ping on rollout plan: can we canary for 24h and then ramp if no stale-read? config in console: rollout: canary=1%, metrics: kv.stale_reads.
Tim: yep. I'll open PR and link to this thread. assigning to me + @Anika for tests.
Sasha: great. low-risk hotfix, leaving in prod overnight to validate. will post logs if it reappears. :thumbsup:
